extracted.intended_audience: medical students, bacteriologists, histologists, and laboratory technicians performing staining and tissue-preparation procedures
extracted.subtask_short: preparing bacteriological stains and staining methods
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory protocols for preparing staining solutions and for demonstrating bacterial and tissue structures (capsules, flagella, spores, acid-fast bacilli) and for preparing tissue sections by freezing or paraffin methods. Includes reagent formulations, timings, temperatures, fixation/decolourisation steps, and handling/storage guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise measurement and preparation of stain solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh out and dissolve specified quantities of dyes and reagents in specified solvents (examples: "Methylene-blue 1.5 grammes ... Distilled water 100.0 c.c.", "Gentian violet 2.25 grammes ...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact formulations given (weights, volumes, solvents), mix in the stated order, and when indicated add absolute alcohol or other solvents. Many entries conclude simply with the instruction: "Filter."

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter all prepared stains and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly every prepared solution or mixed stain is followed by the single imperative 'Filter.' Ensure removal of undissolved particles before storage or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow certain stains/mixtures to stand or mature for specified times
rubrics_metrics.description: Many stains must 'stand' or 'mature' before use (e.g., haematoxylin: mix components and 'allow the mixture to stand forty-eight hours...'; haematoxylin then 'Allow the stain to stand for one month exposed to light').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe specified resting/maturation times (hours, days, weeks) to develop proper staining properties; example: MacConkey stain: 'Allow the stain to stand for two weeks before use.' Some mordants/stains are at their best after several days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Store stains appropriately and respect stated shelf-life/instability
rubrics_metrics.description: Store in a dark place or amber glass bottle when indicated and note instability (e.g., 'this stain deteriorates after about six months'; 'This solution will not keep longer than 14 days').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow storage instructions (dark/amber containers, cool place) and discard or remake unstable solutions after their recommended life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare films for certain blood stains dry but unfixed
rubrics_metrics.description: For Jenner's and Leishman's stains: 'Prepare film, dry, but do not fix.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fix the film before staining because the stain's methylic alcohol component will fix the film during staining (Jenner: allow stain 3 minutes; Leishman: 30 seconds then dilute and allow further action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix films by flaming (standard and heavier for spores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard fixation: 'Fix by passing thrice through the Bunsen flame.' For spores: 'pass the cover-slip film fifteen or thirty times through the flame instead of only three.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust number of flame passes according to target (more flaming to allow stain penetration of resistant spores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentle and careful sample/emulsion handling to preserve delicate structures
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing cultures for flagella demonstration: 'Emulsify... in a watch-glass, by gently moving the spatula to and fro... Do not rub up the growth on the side of the watch-glass... Spread a thin film... using no force, but rather leading the drop... Allow the film to dry in the air, properly protected from falling dust.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle material gently to avoid damaging fragile structures (flagella); use freshly flamed cover-slips and protect drying films from dust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct culture age/conditions for demonstration of structures
rubrics_metrics.description: For flagella: 'smear agar cultures, twelve to eighteen hours old if incubated at 37 deg. C, twenty-four to thirty hours if incubated at 22 deg. C.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select cultivation age and incubation temperature appropriate to the method to maximise successful demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steam-warm mordants and stains for specified times
rubrics_metrics.description: Many methods require warming until 'steam rises' and holding for a fixed time (e.g., Muir's modified Pitfield: steam mordant two minutes; many flagella and mordant steps: 'allow the steaming mordant to remain in contact... two minutes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heat by holding above flame until steaming and time carefully; avoid overheating beyond instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and use appropriate mordant-stain combinations and fresh preparations when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific mordant compositions and stain mixes are given (e.g., Loeffler's mordant 'must be freshly prepared'; Muir's mordant forms a precipitate that must settle and be centrifuged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prescribed mordant and stain pairings; prepare fresh solutions when the method specifies and re-centrifuge or refresh as instructed for reproducible results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decolourise carefully and monitor until desired clearing is achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Example (Gram's): 'Wash with alcohol until no more colour is discharged and the alcohol runs away clear and colourless.' Ziehl-Neelsen: 'Decolourise by dipping in sulphuric acid, 25 per cent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply decolourising agents cautiously and check visually or microscopically; choose the decolouriser (alcohol, acetone/alcohol mix, acids) and time according to the method and organism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterstain lightly with the appropriate counterstain
rubrics_metrics.description: After primary staining and decolourisation many methods call for a light counterstain, e.g., 'Counterstain very lightly with aqueous solution of Neutral Red' or 'counterstain in weak methylene-blue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed counterstain and apply lightly to provide contrast without overwhelming the primary stain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific spore-staining options: single or double stain techniques and suitable decolourisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Single stain: increased flaming in fixation then stain normally. Double stain: hot carbol-fuchsin for twenty minutes, wash, 'Decolourise in alcohol, 2 parts; acetic acid, 1 per cent., 1 part' to remove stain from everything but spores, then counterstain in weak methylene-blue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select single vs double method depending on spore resistance; adjust fixation intensity and decolourisation reagents (sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid in alcohol) per organism and age of spores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-heating in hot stain procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ziehl-Neelsen: 'Stain in hot carbol-fuchsin ... for five to ten minutes. (This stains everything on the film.) Avoid over-heating.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heat sufficiently to assist staining but avoid overheating which can damage specimens or produce artefacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated microscopic examination between differentiating steps where recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Some methods advise: 'To obtain the best differentiation the preparation should be repeatedly examined microscopically (with a 1/6-inch objective) between steps...' (e.g., modified Gram-Weigert, Wheal and Chown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the preparation under the microscope during differentiation steps to stop at optimal contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose freezing or paraffin methods for tissue sections and adhere to sample size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are prepared by either the freezing method or the paraffin method. Tissue pieces should be '2 to 5 mm. cubes when possible, but in any case not exceeding half a centimetre in thickness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select technique based on priority (demonstrate bacteria vs preserve tissue morphology) and cut small blocks for consistent sectioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixation: use specified fixing fluids and use a large excess of fluid
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixation by causing cellular death so elements retain shape; fixing fluids include 'Absolute alcohol; corrosive sublimate, saturated aqueous solution; formaldehyde, 4 per cent. aqueous solution.' 'Lang's corrosive sublimate solution is decidedly the best all-round "fixative."' 'In both these processes a large excess of fluid should always be used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate fixative (Lang's corrosive sublimate recommended) and immerse tissue in a large excess of fixing fluid for the specified duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardening/dehydration: graded alcohol series with sufficient volumes and times
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardening rendered by passing tissues through alcohols of gradually increasing strength: '30 per cent. alcohol, 50 per cent. alcohol, 75 per cent. alcohol, 90 per cent. alcohol, absolute alcohol.' Times per step are given (generally twelve to twenty-four hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the graded alcohol series with large excess volumes and follow timing to avoid incomplete hardening or over-shrinkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearing and infiltration for paraffin embedding: chloroform/alcohol layering and timed paraffin infiltration
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearing: float a layer of absolute alcohol on chloroform and when tissues have sunk transfer to pure chloroform for 6–24 hours. Infiltration: place cleared tissues in chloroform with paraffin wax ~24 hours, then in pure melted paraffin in a bath 2°C above melting-point for ~4–6 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the staged clearing and infiltration durations, using the specified temperatures and agitation, to ensure complete paraffin impregnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use paraffin of appropriate melting point and embed correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: The paraffin used should have a melting-point of not more than 58 deg. C. For all ordinary purposes 54 deg. C. will be found quite high enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select paraffin within the recommended melting-point range to avoid thermal damage during embedding and sectioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed in moulds and cool blocks properly; trim maintaining rectangular shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Imbed in fresh paraffin in a metal (or paper) mould using L-shaped pieces to form troughs, cool in cold water, 'When the block is cold, break off the metal L's; trim off the excess of paraffin from around the tissue, taking care to retain the rectangular shape.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the described moulding and cooling technique to produce blocks suitable for sectioning; trim carefully to preserve block geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gum impregnation and freezing microtome technique for frozen sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Impregnate tissues with mucilage (gum arabic 5 g, saccharose 1 g, boric acid 1 g in 100 c.c. water) for 12–24 hours, freeze with ether or carbon dioxide, cut sections and float off knife into tepid water for ~1 hour to dissolve out gum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the gum impregnation recipe and freezing steps; allow sufficient time to dissolve gum from sections before further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use non-alkaline distilled water when specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Some preparations specify 'Distilled water (non-alkaline)' (e.g., Jenner's stain component).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to water quality (non-alkaline distilled) since alkalinity can affect precipitate formation and stain behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful mixing and evaporation control for precipitation-based stains
rubrics_metrics.description: When mixing methylene blue and eosin: 'Add B to A very slowly, stirring all the time. A viscous precipitate forms...' and on evaporation 'When a paste begins to form scrape and break up occasionally. (On no account must the paste be allowed to fuse.)' Then grind to amorphous powder and dissolve in methylic alcohol, allowing several days for true solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add reagents slowly to control precipitate formation, regulate evaporation temperature (water bath at 55°C), prevent fusion of paste, and allow sufficient time for dissolution of final product.
